title: The Influence of the Substrate and of Environmental Conditions on the Performance of Lime-Based Mortars: Paimogo Fort, a Case Study
content: In order to revitalize and preserve the Paimogo Fort, a Portuguese coastline military fortification built in 1674 and classified of public interest since 1957, several lime-based repair rendering mortars were developed, considering the compatibility requirements with the pre-existing ones. In this investigation the different lime-based mortars compositions proposed are briefly described and their main physical and mechanical characteristics are analysed in successive ages (28, 90 and 180 days). Furthermore, some applications of the same mortars’ compositions on different porous substrates were carried out and their performances were compared in laboratory and in situ conditions. Finally, the possible degradation mechanism and the impact of the composition, interaction with the substrate and climatic and environmental conditions on the durability of the mortars are discussed. The main outcomes show that mortars with some content of quicklime conduct to a balanced solution for the restoration work of the Fort; however, when applied on very absorbent substrates, this type of compositions can lead to a decrease of adhesion between the mortar and the substrate.
